Both moves were smaller in magnitude than the historical average absolute first-session move of [[fact:base.mean_abs_move|8.9%]], with the close-to-close decline just [[fact:reaction.vs_hist_move|0.4x]] that average. The options-implied move is not available, so the reaction cannot be compared with what options had priced in.
- The pattern was **[[fact:reaction.pattern|dip-and-recover]]**: shares recovered part of the opening loss during the session and were down [[fact:reaction.day5_pct|-1.2%]] cumulatively by the fifth session. That recovery followed a [[fact:px.runup_into_print|-8.1%]] decline into the print, but it did not fully erase the earnings loss.
- Across [[fact:base.n_events|12]] past prints, only [[fact:base.p_up_day1|25%]] rose in the first session, and average drift from the first to the fifth session was [[fact:base.drift_5d|-0.3%]]. The narrowing loss was stronger than that slightly negative historical drift, but the history offers little support for assuming the recovery will continue.

section.title: Language and disclosure
section.markdown:
- **Tone:** Management’s tone was model-classified as [[fact:lang.tone|balanced]], but the normalized hedge-word rate rose to [[fact:lang.hedge_rate|12.40]] from [[fact:lang.hedge_rate_prior|10.30]], a reported increase of [[fact:lang.hedge_rate_change|2.11]]. The release paired progress in performance sports with an acknowledgment that Sportswear, Jordan Brand and Greater China still need work. The earnings call transcript is not available, so the language comparison does not extend to Q&A evasiveness or analyst question themes.
- **KPIs:** The release added [[fact:lang.kpis_added|inventories]] versus the prior quarter and dropped [[fact:lang.kpis_dropped|none]]. Inventory is worth tracking as NIKE repositions those businesses: management attributed the movement primarily to product mix, so it is not, on its own, evidence of stronger sell-through.
- **Risk factors:** The filing comparison shows [[fact:filing.risk_paragraphs_added|20]] paragraphs added and [[fact:filing.risk_paragraphs_removed|11]] removed. Trade protectionism was already discussed in the prior text; the updated excerpt explicitly flags that tariffs and retaliation have already had negative effects and that alternative sourcing may carry lasting costs. That makes trade exposure a risk to margin recovery. The excerpts do not establish that the sourcing risks discussed in the removed text disappeared.
- **Material 8-Ks:** The filing review flags [[fact:filing.material_8k_count|6]] events: the earnings-day filing concerned [[fact:filing.material_8k_0|Exit or restructuring costs]], and the remaining filings concerned director or officer departures or appointments. Pace is the clearest earnings read-through: NIKE disclosed [[fact:pr.guide_pace_cumulative_savings|$2.50B]] in expected cumulative savings before charges and any reinvestment, against [[fact:pr.guide_pace_pre_tax_charges|$1.00B]] in expected pre-tax charges, with [[fact:pr.guide_pace_charges_expected_to_be_recognized|$300.0M]] expected to be recognized in FY2027. The headline savings figure is not a net earnings benefit; the timing of realized savings and the amount reinvested matter for how much reaches earnings.

section.title: The print vs expectations
section.markdown:
- **EPS beat, revenue missed.** Q1 FY2027 reported EPS was [[fact:actual.eps|$0.48]] versus mean consensus of [[fact:consensus.eps_mean|$0.43]], a [[fact:surprise.eps_pct|+10.8%]] surprise. Revenue was [[fact:actual.revenue|$11.21B]] versus [[fact:consensus.revenue_mean|$11.32B]], a [[fact:surprise.revenue_pct|-0.9%]] surprise. The beat was in earnings, not sales, so the print offers more evidence of margin and cost progress than of a demand recovery.
- **Management described the quarter as in line with its own expectations**, citing improved gross margin and disciplined cost management. The supplied materials do not include a numerical prior Q1 guide, so the result cannot be benchmarked against one.
- **FY2027 outlook:** NIKE expects revenue to decline and gave an adjusted diluted EPS midpoint of [[fact:pr.guide_adjusted_diluted_eps|$1.25]]. The supplied release excerpt provides no standalone Q2 guide or comparable prior FY2027 guide and does not characterize the outlook as raised or lowered. The adjusted EPS outlook excludes Pace-related restructuring expenses; NIKE expects to recognize [[fact:pr.guide_pace_charges_expected_to_be_recognized|$300.0M]] in Pace charges in FY2027.

section.title: Quality of the print
section.markdown:
- **Period and EPS basis:** The XBRL figures cover [[fact:print.period|FY2027 Q1]], ended [[fact:print.period_end|2026-08-31]]. GAAP diluted EPS was [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap|$0.48]] versus [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap_py|$0.49]] a year earlier. The supplied adjusted-minus-GAAP gap was [[fact:quality.nongaap_gap|$0.00]]: EPS beat consensus but did not grow year over year.
- **Margin improvement cushioned weaker sales.** Revenue fell [[fact:print.revenue_yoy|-4.3%]] year over year. Gross margin rose to [[fact:print.gross_margin|42.8%]] from [[fact:print.gross_margin_py|42.2%]], primarily on lower warehousing and logistics costs, but gross profit still fell to [[fact:print.gross_profit|$4.80B]] from [[fact:print.gross_profit_py|$4.94B]]. Gross margin has also recovered from [[fact:quality.gm_trend_start|40.6%]] in Q2 FY2026. Pretax income was broadly flat at [[fact:print.pretax_income|$921.0M]] versus [[fact:print.pretax_income_py|$922.0M]]. A higher effective tax rate of [[fact:print.tax_rate|22.7%]] versus [[fact:print.tax_rate_py|21.1%]] weighed on net income, and a higher diluted share count added pressure to EPS. A full EPS bridge, including the non-operating contribution, is unavailable without the full income statement in XBRL.
- **Cash flow lagged earnings.** Operating cash flow was [[fact:quality.cfo|$135.0M]] against net income of [[fact:print.net_income|$712.0M]], for cash conversion of [[fact:quality.cash_conversion|0.2x]]. Accruals were [[fact:quality.accruals_pct_rev|5.1%]] of revenue, and free cash flow was [[fact:quality.fcf|$-64.0M]] after capex of [[fact:quality.capex|$199.0M]]. DSO was [[fact:quality.dso|43 days]], and the balance used for DSO rose to [[fact:quality.dso_balance|$5.24B]] from [[fact:quality.dso_balance_py|$4.96B]] despite lower sales. That makes collections worth monitoring, but the supplied figures do not establish how much receivables contributed to the cash shortfall. Inventory days and deferred revenue are not available in the supplied figures.

section.markdown:
- **Consensus is above AMD’s revenue guide.** The market expects Q3 revenue of [[fact:consensus.revenue_mean|$13.10B]] and EPS of [[fact:consensus.eps_mean|$1.95]]. Clearing the company’s revenue midpoint alone would not clear consensus.
- **An EPS beat is familiar.** AMD beat EPS estimates in [[fact:hist.eps_beat_rate|88%]] of the last [[fact:hist.n_quarters|8]] quarters, with an average surprise of [[fact:hist.avg_eps_surprise_pct|+3.7%]]. In Q2, revenue came in [[fact:guidance.rev_vs_own_guide|+3.0%]] above AMD’s own midpoint, while non-GAAP gross margin matched guidance. A clean beat would clear both consensus means, meet or exceed the guided margin, and show that operating performance drove the EPS upside. A forward outlook that supports the stronger result would make the beat more convincing.
- **The mean is visible; the range and direction are not.** The EPS median, high, low, estimate count and dispersion are unavailable without FINNHUB_API_KEY or FMP premium analyst-estimates data. Short- and longer-window EPS revisions are unavailable without daily consensus snapshots or a paid estimate history, so it is not possible to tell whether the bar has been rising or falling.

section.markdown:
- **AMD has sold off more than the market or tech.** Over the recent trading window, AMD returned [[fact:px.runup_20d|-26.1%]], versus [[fact:px.runup_20d_spy|-2.9%]] for SPY and [[fact:px.runup_20d_xlk|-13.3%]] for XLK. - **Historical moves are sizable; the options hurdle is unknown.** Across [[fact:base.n_events|12]] prior prints, the absolute first-session move averaged [[fact:base.mean_abs_move|8.0%]] and had a median of [[fact:base.median_abs_move|6.7%]]. Shares rose in {{+fact:base.p_up_day1}} of those events and in [[fact:base.p_up_given_beat|50%]] of EPS beats. The options-implied move is unavailable without historical options data, so it cannot be compared with those realized moves.
- **Short positioning looks light.** Short interest was [[fact:pos.short_pct_float|2.4%]] of float, with [[fact:pos.days_to_cover|2 days]] to cover and a month-over-month change of [[fact:pos.short_change_pct|-1.7%]]. That offers limited evidence for a squeeze-driven reaction. Institutional holding changes are unavailable because institutional holdings filings are not ingested.
- **Valuation has compressed, but the bar for a sustained positive reaction still looks high.** Trailing GAAP P/E is [[fact:val.pe_ttm|120.0x]], below its historical median of [[fact:val.pe_ttm_3y_median|196.5x]]. The multiple on annualized next-quarter consensus EPS is [[fact:val.pe_fwd_run_rate|59.9x]], a run-rate measure rather than a full-year forward estimate. With [[fact:ctx.season_beat_rate|80%]] of [[fact:ctx.season_n|51]] recent reporters beating EPS, a headline beat alone is unlikely to stand out. The selloff has lowered the sentiment bar, but the multiple leaves investors looking for margin support and a forward outlook that sustains the earnings trajectory.

The note sets out a test for a clean beat without giving the Q2 baseline: comps rose 2.2%, with average check up 1.2% and transactions up 1.0%, while restaurant-level margin fell to 25.2% from 27.4% a year earlier. Reported GAAP and adjusted EPS were both flat year over year despite lower net income and a lower diluted share count.

The event-risk discussion gives only the size of historical moves. Day one was positive in 58% of the 12 events (55% after shrinkage toward 50%) and in 75% of the eight EPS beats in that sample. Shares opened down [[fact:reaction.gap_pct|-4.2%]], closed the first session at [[fact:reaction.day1_pct|-2.7%]], and ended the window at [[fact:reaction.day5_pct|-1.7%]] versus the pre-print close. The partial rebound fits the base case.

Q4 AI semiconductor revenue guidance of [[fact:pr.guide_ai_semiconductor_revenue|$21.70B]] versus Q3’s [[fact:pr.ai_semiconductor_revenue|$16.70B]] makes shipment timing and margin under the new mix more important than the modest EPS beat.

scenarios.narrative: A larger rebound would have required investors to see the Q4 AI ramp as backed by firm customer schedules, with Q3 cash generation reinforcing confidence that incremental sales would convert to cash.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.narrative: The modest rebound is consistent with a routine EPS beat and a larger AI outlook that investors still wanted to see delivered. The stock pared its loss without reclaiming the pre-print close.

scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.narrative: A renewed selloff would have required investors to see material risk of AI shipments slipping or of the richer revenue mix putting more pressure on margins than the Q4 guide implied.

what_would_change_view: Firm customer deployment schedules and evidence of margin resilience would strengthen confidence in the Q4 ramp; shipment deferrals or greater mix pressure would weaken it.
Daily consensus snapshots or paid estimate history are unavailable; post-print EPS revisions would help test whether the rebound coincided with higher earnings expectations.

What mix assumptions underpin Q4’s non-GAAP operating margin guide, and how sensitive is it to the timing of AI shipments?
What drove the year-over-year decline in current deferred revenue, and how much reflects billing timing rather than underlying software demand?

issues.detail: The stated 22% does not reconcile to the bridge on a net basis: $0.15 + $0.23 − $0.01 = $0.37, or about 20% of the $1.83 EPS increase. The fact sheet separately lists 22%; clarify the calculation before presenting it as the net share.

The Q4 outlook omits the year-over-year comparisons that put the AI ramp in context: management guided to 93% total revenue growth and 236% AI semiconductor revenue growth, versus 221% AI growth in Q3. The 66% non-GAAP operating margin guide is flat year over year but below Q3's actual margin of about 67.9%.

The reaction section gives the historical move size but omits the more relevant directional baseline: only 50% of the 12 measured EPS beats were followed by a positive day-one move. A decline after a beat was not unusual in this sample.

The +2.5% EPS surprise was close to Broadcom's historical average of +2.6%, and the company beat in all eight quarters in the EPS history. This context distinguishes a typical beat from an unusually strong one.

The assertion that the forward outlook 'matters more' than the revenue beat is an editorial ranking, not a conclusion established by the facts. The reported guidance and AI revenue figures support describing the ramp without ranking its importance.
'Working capital merits watching' is advice about what readers should monitor. State the observed working-capital changes and their limits without the directive.

The note presents the day-five return without flagging that its supplied August 27 as-of date precedes the fifth trading session after the August 26 after-close release.

The note omits the October 15 close and valuation context. The 22.5x trailing GAAP P/E versus a 42.0x three-year median is relevant to a portfolio manager, with the caveat that the quarter's non-operating gains inflate the trailing EPS denominator.

section.title: Market reaction
section.markdown:
CRM opened up [[fact:reaction.gap_pct|+11.9%]] and extended the gain to [[fact:reaction.day1_pct|+22.6%]] close to close—a gap-and-go reaction. The opening gap alone exceeded the historical average absolute earnings-day move of [[fact:base.mean_abs_move|7.3%]]; the full session move was [[fact:reaction.vs_hist_move|3.1x]] that average. The options-implied move is not available in the supplied data, so the reaction can be benchmarked against history but not against what options priced in.

CRM had rallied [[fact:px.runup_into_print|+9.2%]] into the print, outperforming SPY by [[fact:px.runup_vs_spy_into_print|+4.1%]] but lagging XLK on a relative basis ([[fact:px.runup_vs_sector_into_print|-0.6%]]). The pre-print rally was therefore less distinctive against tech than against the broad market.

The cumulative gain reached [[fact:reaction.day5_pct|+25.0%]] by the fifth session, extending rather than reversing the initial jump. Historical drift from the first to the fifth session averaged just [[fact:base.drift_5d|+0.4%]] across [[fact:base.n_events|12]] past prints, offering little basis to extrapolate the initial surge.

section.title: The print vs expectations
section.markdown:
Salesforce reported adjusted EPS of [[fact:actual.eps|$5.90]] versus mean consensus of [[fact:consensus.eps_mean|$3.27]], a [[fact:surprise.eps_pct|+80.4%]] beat. XBRL total revenue was [[fact:print.revenue|$11.35B]]. The release-derived field labeled total revenue ([[fact:pr.revenue|$10.80B]]) instead matches the excerpt’s subscription and support figure. Revenue consensus and Salesforce’s prior Q2 guidance are unavailable, so neither a revenue surprise nor performance against the company’s own guide can be established.

Salesforce **initiated** Q3 revenue, EPS and cRPO guidance; it did not characterize the Q3 outlook as a raise or cut. It explicitly **raised** full-year revenue guidance, citing stronger organic growth and contributions from pending acquisitions, partly offset by a smaller currency tailwind. The updated outlook is conditional on those deals closing, while cRPO guidance excludes them. Full-year adjusted operating margin guidance was unchanged. For the stock reaction, the distinction is that the EPS beat was clear, but the full-year revenue raise was not entirely organic.

section.title: Quality of the print
section.markdown:
The XBRL figures cover **[[fact:print.period|FY2027 Q2]]**, ended [[fact:print.period_end|2026-07-31]]. GAAP diluted EPS rose to [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap|$4.29]] from [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap_py|$1.96]]. Adjusted EPS of [[fact:actual.eps|$5.90]] exceeded GAAP EPS by [[fact:quality.nongaap_gap|$1.61]], equivalent to [[fact:quality.nongaap_gap_pct|+37.5%]] of GAAP EPS.

Revenue grew [[fact:print.revenue_yoy|+10.8%]] year over year, but operating income was flat at [[fact:print.operating_income|$2.33B]]. In the modeled GAAP EPS bridge, revenue growth contributed [[fact:quality.eps_from_revenue|$0.21]], offset by a margin effect of [[fact:quality.eps_from_operating_margin|$-0.21]]. Non-operating items were the largest contributor at [[fact:quality.eps_from_non_operating|$1.75]], followed by a lower diluted share count at [[fact:quality.eps_from_share_count|$0.63]]; the higher tax rate contributed [[fact:quality.eps_from_tax_rate|$-0.05]]. Gross margin fell to [[fact:print.gross_margin|76.7%]] from [[fact:print.gross_margin_py|78.1%]] a year earlier, and operating margin fell to [[fact:print.operating_margin|20.5%]] from [[fact:print.operating_margin_py|22.8%]]. The GAAP EPS growth therefore did not reflect stronger operating profitability.

Operating cash flow of [[fact:quality.cfo|$1.27B]] translated to [[fact:quality.cash_conversion|0.4x]] of net income, with free cash flow of [[fact:quality.fcf|$1.10B]]. Net income less operating cash flow was [[fact:quality.accruals_pct_rev|19.9%]] of revenue, so reported earnings growth was not matched by cash conversion in the quarter. DSO was [[fact:quality.dso|51 days]]; the underlying receivables balance rose to [[fact:quality.dso_balance|$6.32B]] from [[fact:quality.dso_balance_py|$5.60B]], but prior-year DSO is unavailable. Current deferred revenue grew [[fact:quality.deferred_revenue_yoy|+13.5%]] year over year to [[fact:quality.deferred_revenue|$18.79B]]. Inventory days are unavailable.

setup: Provider-basis EPS beat consensus by [[fact:surprise.eps_pct|+80.4%]]. XBRL revenue grew [[fact:print.revenue_yoy|+10.8%]] year over year; revenue consensus (consensus.revenue_mean) is unavailable, so a sales beat cannot be established.
CRM rose [[fact:reaction.day1_pct|+22.6%]] on the first session and reached [[fact:reaction.day5_pct|+25.0%]] cumulatively by the fifth, extending the initial jump only modestly.

Operating income was flat year over year despite revenue growth. Non-operating items were the largest contributor to modeled GAAP EPS growth, and cash conversion was [[fact:quality.cash_conversion|0.4x]].

scenarios.narrative: A stronger follow-through would require investors to read deferred revenue growth as evidence of durable demand and expect that growth to translate into better margins and cash flow.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.narrative: The first-session jump absorbs most of the EPS surprise. Deferred revenue growth supports modest follow-through, but flat operating income limits further gains; the observed path fits this case.

scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.narrative: A reversal would require investors to put more weight on margin compression and weak cash conversion than on the headline beat, especially if non-operating gains prove transitory.

what_would_change_view: Evidence that deferred revenue growth is converting into stronger operating margins and cash flow would make the rally more fundamentally supported.
A reconciliation showing that the largest non-operating gains are unlikely to recur, alongside persistent cash conversion weakness, would make the earnings uplift less durable.
questions_for_call: What drove the largest non-operating gains, and which components should analysts treat as recurring?
Why did operating income remain flat despite revenue growth, and what would restore operating leverage?
How much of the cash conversion shortfall reflects collection timing versus a more persistent working-capital drag?
key_risks: The modeled GAAP EPS bridge does not explain the provider-basis surprise; conflating the two could overstate what is known about the beat’s quality.
Deferred revenue growth does not establish when cash will be collected or whether incremental revenue will carry better margins.

issues.detail: Quantify the FY27 revenue raise: the new range is $46.1–$46.4B, up $200M ($300M in constant currency), reflecting $100M of organic growth and $200M from pending acquisitions, offset by a $100M FX headwind. The note identifies the drivers but does not show their relative size.

Add two material operating results from the release: Informatica contributed $456M to Q2 revenue, and cRPO reached $33.5B, with growth accelerating to 14% year over year in constant currency. These figures distinguish acquisition-supported revenue growth from the reported backlog trend.

Balance the weak cash-conversion discussion with the release's year-over-year growth figures: operating cash flow rose 71% and free cash flow rose 81%. The 0.4x conversion ratio describes cash flow relative to net income, not a lack of cash-flow growth.
“Investors should not assume the KPI lineup was unchanged” is advice language. State instead that changes to the KPI lineup could not be verified from the supplied materials.

The note benchmarks the size of the move but omits the historical directional base rate: CRM rose on day one after only 45% of the 11 prior EPS beats, versus 50% across all 12 measured prints. That context helps distinguish the large EPS beat from the unusually strong stock response.

problems: The note twice attributes a benefit to GAAP EPS and gross margin to tariff refunds, including an assertion that Apple said so. Neither the cited facts nor a supplied quotation supports that claim.

The 25% bull, 55% base, and 20% bear weights have no stated basis or forecast horizon. The scenarios describe possible investor interpretations but give no measurable thresholds for inventory, margins, or guidance that would change the view.

The expectation section initially puts $2.10 GAAP EPS alongside the $1.99 consensus, then later uses the correct provider-series comparison of $2.05 versus $1.99. Lead with the provider-series comparison and keep the GAAP result separate; the exact consensus EPS basis is not documented.

The reaction analysis misses a source-timing inconsistency: the fifth-session return is labeled as of November 3, one day after the November 2 after-close release. Flag it for verification before relying on it. Also distinguish the realized cumulative return from the pre-event close from the historical drift measured from day 1 to day 5.

The opening gap is compared with a historical close-to-close move, which is not like-for-like. The 86% earnings-season beat rate is a November 20 snapshot and does not establish what investors knew before the November 2 print.

The full-cycle update omits the November 2 after-close timestamp, the November 20 close and benchmark-relative performance, and notable capital-return and positioning facts: $24.30B in repurchases and $127M in insider sales, 75% under 10b5-1 plans. It also leaves peer valuation and institutional positioning gaps unstated.

The product and geography discussion does not quantify the sequential moves that matter to the thesis: iPhone and Services rose, while Greater China fell from $18.82B to $17.54B. The long raw KPI lists add clutter without clarifying which disclosures actually changed.

Across [[fact:base.n_events|12]] past prints, Apple rose on the first session only [[fact:base.p_up_day1|33%]] of the time, but averaged [[fact:base.drift_5d|+1.7%]] from the first close through the fifth. This print followed that historical tendency toward later strength, though the small sample makes the average a weak predictor.

section.title: The print vs expectations
section.markdown:
- **Both headline metrics beat consensus on the provider basis.** EPS of [[fact:actual.eps|$2.05]] versus [[fact:consensus.eps_mean|$1.99]] was a [[fact:surprise.eps_pct|+3.0%]] surprise. Revenue of [[fact:actual.revenue|$114.48B]] versus [[fact:consensus.revenue_mean|$113.40B]] was a [[fact:surprise.revenue_pct|+0.9%]] surprise. The EPS beat was larger than the revenue beat, but Apple’s release separately reported GAAP diluted EPS of [[fact:pr.gaap_diluted_eps|$2.10]] and revenue of [[fact:pr.revenue|$114.50B]]. The GAAP EPS figure is not the basis for the consensus comparison.
- **Guidance is unverified.** The supplied release excerpt does not state Apple’s prior guidance for the reported quarter or provide a next-period outlook. The print therefore cannot be benchmarked against Apple’s own guide, and the next-period outlook cannot be compared with any prior guide. The excerpt does not say guidance was raised or lowered; that is not evidence it was unchanged.

section.title: Quality of the print
section.markdown:
- **EPS basis and drivers.** The XBRL figures refer to [[fact:print.period|FY2026 Q4]], ended [[fact:print.period_end|2026-09-26]]. GAAP diluted EPS rose to [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap|$2.10]] from [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap_py|$1.84]]. Provider-basis EPS minus GAAP diluted EPS was [[fact:quality.nongaap_gap|$-0.05]]. Apple said tariff refunds benefited GAAP EPS and gross margin, but the supplied material does not reconcile the provider figure to GAAP, so the gap cannot be attributed to the refunds. Revenue growth of [[fact:print.revenue_yoy|+11.7%]] supported higher operating income despite operating margin falling to [[fact:print.operating_margin|31.1%]] from [[fact:print.operating_margin_py|31.6%]]. Net non-operating items contributed more than a year earlier, and the effective tax rate fell to [[fact:print.tax_rate|15.0%]] from [[fact:print.tax_rate_py|16.3%]]. The XBRL diluted-share values are negative, making the modeled EPS bridge unreliable and preventing a defensible estimate of the share-count contribution.
- **Margin and cash conversion.** Gross margin of [[fact:print.gross_margin|47.9%]] was above the year-ago [[fact:print.gross_margin_py|47.2%]] but below FY2026 Q1’s [[fact:quality.gm_trend_start|48.2%]], even with the tariff-refund benefit. Operating cash flow of [[fact:quality.cfo|$28.10B]] lagged net income of [[fact:print.net_income|$30.71B]], leaving cash conversion at [[fact:quality.cash_conversion|0.9x]] and accruals at [[fact:quality.accruals_pct_rev|2.3%]] of revenue. Free cash flow was [[fact:quality.fcf|$25.86B]].
- **Working capital.** DSO was [[fact:quality.dso|35 days]]; the underlying balance grew more slowly than revenue year over year. Inventory days were [[fact:quality.inventory_days|22 days]], and the inventory balance rose to [[fact:quality.inventory_days_balance|$14.54B]] from [[fact:quality.inventory_days_balance_py|$5.72B]], outpacing sales growth. That build warrants monitoring for sell-through but does not by itself establish weaker demand. Current deferred revenue grew [[fact:quality.deferred_revenue_yoy|+6.4%]] year over year.

section.title: The expectation bar
section.markdown:
Pre-print consensus was [[fact:consensus.revenue_mean|$113.40B]] in revenue and [[fact:consensus.eps_mean|$1.99]] in EPS. Apple reported [[fact:pr.revenue|$114.50B]] in revenue and [[fact:pr.gaap_diluted_eps|$2.10]] in GAAP diluted EPS. Revenue cleared the mean, and reported EPS was above the quoted mean, though the consensus EPS basis is not specified. The prior quarter’s release is the relevant source for Apple’s outlook for the reported quarter, but the supplied prior-release data contain only actuals, so performance against management’s own bar cannot be assessed.

Apple’s EPS beat rate was [[fact:hist.eps_beat_rate|100%]] across [[fact:hist.n_quarters|8]] quarters, with an average surprise of [[fact:hist.avg_eps_surprise_pct|+4.8%]]. That record makes a routine EPS beat less informative. A clean beat would pair above-consensus sales with a like-for-like EPS beat supported by operating performance rather than one-off benefits. Gross margin fell to [[fact:pr.gross_margin|47.9%]] from [[fact:pr_prior.gross_margin|50.1%]] sequentially, so the headline beats alone do not establish margin strength. An above-plan contribution from iPhone or Services would strengthen the read-through, but product-level expectations are not supplied.

The EPS median, high and low estimates, estimate count, and dispersion are unavailable without Finnhub or FMP premium analyst-estimates data. EPS revisions across the requested windows are also unavailable without daily consensus snapshots or a paid estimate history. The mean therefore does not show how demanding the upper end of expectations was or whether the bar had been rising into the print.

section.title: What is priced in
section.markdown:
Into the print, Apple rose [[fact:px.runup_into_print|+1.6%]] while SPY fell [[fact:px.runup_20d_spy_into_print|-2.9%]] and XLK fell [[fact:px.runup_20d_xlk_into_print|-13.3%]]. The standout was relative strength: Apple outperformed SPY by [[fact:px.runup_vs_spy_into_print|+4.6%]] and XLK by [[fact:px.runup_vs_sector_into_print|+14.9%]]. The modest absolute gain is less evidence of exuberance than the relative performance is of a demanding setup.

Across [[fact:base.n_events|12]] measured earnings events, the average absolute first-session move was [[fact:base.mean_abs_move|2.4%]] and the median was [[fact:base.median_abs_move|1.6%]]. Shares rose after only [[fact:base.p_up_given_beat|33%]] of EPS beats in the sample, a reminder that clearing consensus has not reliably translated into upside. No pre-print options-implied move is supplied, so the historical moves cannot establish whether options priced a large or small reaction.

Into the print, short interest was [[fact:pos.short_pct_float|1.0%]] of float, with [[fact:pos.days_to_cover|4 days]] to cover. Shares short rose [[fact:pos.short_change_pct|+19.9%]] versus the prior month, but the low share of float argues against a crowded short setup. At the latest close, trailing GAAP P/E was [[fact:val.pe_ttm|38.2x]], above its historical median of [[fact:val.pe_ttm_3y_median|36.5x]] but within the observed range of [[fact:val.pe_ttm_3y_low|30.6x]] to [[fact:val.pe_ttm_3y_high|54.5x]]. That is a post-print valuation snapshot, not the multiple going into earnings.

The latest earnings-season sample had an EPS beat rate of [[fact:ctx.season_beat_rate|86%]] across [[fact:ctx.season_n|51]] reporters, making a beat a weak differentiator in that sample. **The bar looked high for a positive reaction to a routine beat.** Pre-print relative strength and Apple’s history of muted directional responses to EPS beats support that conclusion; the data do not show whether the options market set a high bar for the size of the move.

scenarios.name: base

section.title: Market reaction
section.markdown:
JPM opened up [[fact:reaction.gap_pct|+1.7%]] but gave back the gain and closed down [[fact:reaction.day1_pct|-0.9%]]. Both moves were smaller in absolute terms than the historical average close-to-close earnings move of [[fact:base.mean_abs_move|2.5%]]. The close-to-close move was [[fact:reaction.vs_hist_move|0.3x]] the historical average in magnitude, making this a [[fact:reaction.pattern|muted]] reaction despite the intraday reversal. No options-implied move was supplied.

JPM entered the print down [[fact:px.runup_into_print|-4.0%]], lagging SPY by [[fact:px.runup_vs_spy_into_print|-6.6%]] and XLF by [[fact:px.runup_vs_sector_into_print|-0.9%]] on a relative-return basis. The opening bounce did not hold despite that weak lead-in.

By the fifth session, the cumulative loss had narrowed to [[fact:reaction.day5_pct|-0.2%]]. That partial recovery was consistent with the historical average post-earnings drift of [[fact:base.drift_5d|+0.5%]] from the first to the fifth session, though the sample of [[fact:base.n_events|12]] prior prints offers limited evidence that an initial decline will reverse.

section.title: Language and disclosure
section.markdown:
- **Tone:** The model classified management’s written tone as [[fact:lang.tone|balanced]]. The hedge-word rate in the release and CFO commentary fell to [[fact:lang.hedge_rate|4.27]] from [[fact:lang.hedge_rate_prior|4.82]] (change: [[fact:lang.hedge_rate_change|-0.55]]). The release paired positive commentary on business performance with cautions about inflation, fiscal deficits, rates, asset prices and geopolitics. Less hedging in the written materials is not evidence that management became more confident on the call. No earnings call transcript was uploaded; a licensed transcript or user upload is needed to assess Q&A evasiveness and analyst question themes.
- **KPIs:** The comparison flagged additions: [[fact:lang.kpis_added|asset & wealth management (awm), assets under management (aum), client asset net inflows, commercial & investment bank (cib), consumer & community banking (ccb), corporate, credit costs, return on common equity (roe), return on tangible common equity (rotce), risk-weighted assets (rwa)]]. It flagged removals: [[fact:lang.kpis_dropped|aum, client assets, expense, net charge-offs, net reserve build, provision for credit losses, roe, rotce]]. AUM, ROE and ROTCE appear on both lists, and the current release excerpt still reports expense, net charge-offs and the net reserve build. The flags therefore do not establish that JPMorgan stopped reporting those metrics; they should not be read as reduced visibility into credit costs or expenses.
- **Risk factors:** The filing comparison flagged [[fact:filing.risk_paragraphs_added|24]] paragraphs added and [[fact:filing.risk_paragraphs_removed|21]] removed. The supplied excerpts show refreshed deposit and funding commentary, including a higher estimate of uninsured deposits, primarily reflecting wholesale operating deposits. For investors, the more relevant question is what the deposit mix means for funding stability and costs; the paragraph counts alone do not establish a new risk factor.
- **Material 8-Ks:** The disclosed lookback contains [[fact:filing.material_8k_count|3]] events. The latest was a [[fact:filing.material_8k_0|Director/officer departure or appointment]] event. The earlier filings, in reverse chronological order, covered a [[fact:filing.material_8k_1|Charter/bylaw amendment]] and a [[fact:filing.material_8k_2|Director/officer departure or appointment]] event. The categories identify governance items to review but do not establish their operating or financial impact.

section.title: The print vs expectations
section.markdown:
- JPMorgan missed mean consensus on both measures: provider EPS was [[fact:actual.eps|$5.75]] versus [[fact:consensus.eps_mean|$5.93]] (surprise: [[fact:surprise.eps_pct|-3.0%]]), and reported revenue was [[fact:actual.revenue|$50.17B]] versus [[fact:consensus.revenue_mean|$51.23B]] (surprise: [[fact:surprise.revenue_pct|-2.1%]]).
- The provider EPS matches the release’s EPS excluding net investment securities losses, so the earnings miss persists after that adjustment. The revenue comparison uses reported revenue, not the higher managed-basis figure of [[fact:pr.net_revenue_managed|$50.91B]].
- The supplied release excerpt does not provide company guidance for the reported quarter or current and prior guides for the next period. The print therefore cannot be benchmarked against management’s own guidance, and the excerpt does not establish whether management raised or lowered its outlook.

section.title: Quality of the print
section.markdown:
- The XBRL figures refer to [[fact:print.period|FY2026 Q3]], ended [[fact:print.period_end|2026-09-30]]. GAAP diluted EPS was [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap|$5.57]] versus [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap_py|$5.07]] a year earlier. Excluding net investment securities losses lifted EPS to [[fact:pr.non_gaap_diluted_eps_excluding_net_inves|$5.75]], a gap of [[fact:quality.nongaap_gap|$0.18]] ([[fact:quality.nongaap_gap_pct|+3.2%]] of GAAP EPS).
- Revenue grew [[fact:print.revenue_yoy|+8.1%]] year over year but fell [[fact:print.revenue_qoq|-12.5%]] sequentially. Pretax income rose to [[fact:print.pretax_income|$20.13B]] from [[fact:print.pretax_income_py|$18.74B]], but lagged year-over-year revenue growth, implying modest pretax margin compression. The effective tax rate rose to [[fact:print.tax_rate|24.0%]] from [[fact:print.tax_rate_py|23.2%]], tempering net income growth, while diluted shares fell to [[fact:print.diluted_shares|2,683,000,000]] from [[fact:print.diluted_shares_py|2,767,600,000]], supporting per-share growth. A full EPS bridge, including separate operating and non-operating contributions, requires the full income statement in XBRL.
- Operating cash flow of [[fact:quality.cfo|$33.16B]] was [[fact:quality.cash_conversion|2.2x]] net income, with accruals at [[fact:quality.accruals_pct_rev|-35.6%]] of revenue. Cash flow exceeded earnings, but a bank’s operating cash flow can be affected by balance-sheet movements, so this alone does not establish sustainable cash conversion. DSO, inventory days and deferred-revenue trends are not available in the supplied data and are not primary working-capital indicators for a bank.

section.title: The expectation bar
section.markdown:
**Pre-print consensus:** Mean EPS was [[fact:consensus.eps_mean|$5.93]] and mean revenue was [[fact:consensus.revenue_mean|$51.23B]]. The supplied prior-release figures are Q2 actuals, not Q3 guidance; no quarter-specific company outlook is available in the supplied material. The EPS median, high, low, estimate count and dispersion are unavailable, as is revision history. The means show where the bar was, but not how tightly estimates clustered or whether the bar was rising into the print.

**Beat history:** JPM beat EPS estimates in [[fact:hist.eps_beat_rate|75%]] of the past [[fact:hist.n_quarters|8]] quarters, with an average surprise of [[fact:hist.avg_eps_surprise_pct|+10.1%]]. A narrow EPS beat alone would have been less convincing than an upside surprise backed by revenue.

**What a clean beat required:** EPS and revenue above consensus on comparable reporting bases, with the upside driven by recurring operations rather than one-off gains or unusually light credit provisions. The reported results fell short of that test: GAAP EPS was [[fact:pr.gaap_diluted_eps|$5.57]] and EPS excluding net investment securities losses was [[fact:pr.non_gaap_diluted_eps_excluding_net_inves|$5.75]], both below the published mean. Reported revenue of [[fact:pr.net_revenue_reported|$50.17B]] and managed revenue of [[fact:pr.net_revenue_managed|$50.91B]] were also below the published mean, though the consensus reporting basis is not specified.

section.title: What is priced in
section.markdown:
**Into the print:** JPM fell [[fact:px.runup_into_print|-4.0%]] while SPY gained [[fact:px.runup_20d_spy_into_print|+2.5%]] and XLF fell [[fact:px.runup_20d_xlf_into_print|-3.1%]]. JPM's relative moves were [[fact:px.runup_vs_spy_into_print|-6.6%]] against SPY and [[fact:px.runup_vs_sector_into_print|-0.9%]] against XLF. The stock lagged both, but the much smaller gap against XLF suggests sector weakness explains much of the broad-market underperformance.

**Reaction hurdle:** Across [[fact:base.n_events|12]] measured earnings events, the mean absolute first-day move was [[fact:base.mean_abs_move|2.5%]] and the median was [[fact:base.median_abs_move|1.9%]]. Shares rose after only [[fact:base.p_up_given_beat|40%]] of EPS beats, so a beat alone has not reliably produced a positive reaction. No pre-print options-implied move is supplied, so there is no basis for judging whether options priced a larger or smaller move than usual.

**Positioning and valuation since the print:** Latest short interest was [[fact:pos.short_pct_float|0.9%]] of float, with [[fact:pos.days_to_cover|3 days]] to cover and a month-over-month change in shares short of [[fact:pos.short_change_pct|-1.6%]]. That does not point to a crowded short. JPM trades at [[fact:val.pe_ttm|13.0x]] trailing GAAP earnings versus its historical median of [[fact:val.pe_ttm_3y_median|15.1x]] and within its historical range of [[fact:val.pe_ttm_3y_low|11.0x]] to [[fact:val.pe_ttm_3y_high|22.1x]]. These are post-print readings, not evidence of positioning or valuation on earnings eve.

**Season context and bottom line:** The latest reporting cohort had an EPS beat rate of [[fact:ctx.season_beat_rate|86%]] across [[fact:ctx.season_n|51]] companies. That's current context, not a measure of sentiment going into JPM's report. The pre-print price bar looked relatively low given the pullback, but the hurdle for a positive reaction was higher: JPM's own history suggests that an EPS beat without supporting revenue strength was unlikely to be enough.

issues.detail: The expectation section calls $94.97B a total-revenue consensus, while this section says the consensus basis is unconfirmed. The release reports $95.723B in Q4 total revenue, including $1.850B in membership fees. That would be a 0.8% beat if the consensus is for total revenue; the provider’s 1.2% miss uses net sales instead.

Quantify the disclosed $0.15-per-share tariff benefit, net of partial reinvestment. It accounts for about 71% of the $0.21 headline EPS surprise. Subtracting it leaves $6.60, about 0.9% above consensus, though the estimate basis is unconfirmed and $6.60 is not company-reported adjusted EPS.

The note relies on Q3 for operating performance even though the release provides Q4 results: operating income rose 13.8% to $3.801B from $3.341B, and operating margin on total revenue rose to 3.97% from 3.88%. These figures describe Q4 performance without implying an operating beat against consensus.

The note cites regional unadjusted comps but omits the release’s companywide and digitally enabled figures. Companywide comps were 9.4% unadjusted and 6.7% excluding gasoline-price and FX effects; digitally enabled comps were 19.5% and 19.8%, respectively. Those figures give a fuller picture of demand without establishing a beat against estimates.

The note correctly identifies the 60.3x P/E as using a stale denominator but omits the updated figure available from the release. The $1,102.15 close divided by FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $20.76 implies about 53.1x, below the supplied 59.5x three-year median rather than above it.
The supplied risk excerpts show changes to membership disclosures, staffing, executive roles and cybersecurity oversight, but do not show changes to prior-period financial commentary.

The note calls the $94.97B consensus a total-revenue estimate here but says its definition is unconfirmed in the_print. The facts label it only as revenue consensus. Distinguish the provider’s 1.2% miss using $93.87B in net sales from the conditional 0.8% beat using the release’s $95.723B in total revenue.

The release quantifies the nonrecurring tariff-refund benefit, net of partial reinvestment, at $0.15 per diluted share. Subtracting it gives $6.60, only $0.06 (about 0.9%) above the $6.54 consensus, whose adjustment basis is unconfirmed. A full EPS bridge is unavailable, but that does not preclude quantifying this disclosed item.

The quality discussion relies on Q3 XBRL for operating performance even though the Q4 release shows operating income rising 13.8% to $3.801B from $3.341B, with operating margin rising to about 3.97% from 3.88%. Include those Q4 results as year-over-year context, not as evidence of an operating beat.

The provider’s $6.75 EPS matches reported GAAP EPS, but that numerical match does not establish that the provider did not use a separate adjusted measure. State the match without inferring the provider’s methodology.

The note correctly flags the stale denominator behind the supplied 60.3x P/E, but the release provides updated FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $20.76. At the November 20 close of $1,102.15, that implies about 53.1x, materially below the supplied figure.

The supplied excerpts support updates to membership, staffing, executive roles and cybersecurity oversight, but do not show changes to prior-period financial commentary. Remove that characterization or tie it to specific quoted text.

problems: The market-reaction analysis stops at day 1 even though the fact set runs through November 20. NVDA closed at $125.97 on November 20, about 19% below its $155.46 pre-print close. That materially changes the setup and makes a base case anchored to the first post-earnings close stale.

The scenario probabilities are unexplained, sum to 101%, and have no time horizon. The scenarios describe plausible narratives, but do not specify what evidence on margins, Data Center growth, cash conversion, or estimate revisions would change the view.

The note says management’s prior Q3 guide was not supplied after citing its gross-margin and operating-expense guidance. It should specify that Q3 revenue and EPS targets are missing. It should also qualify the blanket EPS-beat statement because the consensus basis is unknown.

The note invokes sustained Data Center demand without reporting the available segment evidence: Q3 Data Center revenue was $107.60B versus $89.00B in Q2. It also omits Q4 GAAP operating-expense guidance and does not translate the non-GAAP margin step-down into the 340-basis-point change central to the thesis.

The note discusses short interest but omits the available insider-positioning data: $967.6M of reported open-market sales, no purchases, and 2% of sales reported under 10b5-1 plans. These are relevant context, not evidence of insider motive or a directional forecast.

The 15.9x multiple uses the November 20 price and a pre-Q3 EPS denominator, so it is not evidence of the multiple going into the print. A reading below the stated three-year low also warrants a check of the historical window and calculation methodology before drawing a cheapness inference.

The risk-factor comparison predates the Q3 print and should be explicitly dated. The note correctly resolves the conflicting 'gap-down' label using the numerical returns, but comparing the opening gap with a historical close-to-close benchmark is not like-for-like.

issues.detail: The latest release explicitly gives Q3 FY27 guidance: adjusted EPS of $0.62–$0.64, constant-currency net sales growth of 3.0%–3.75%, and constant-currency adjusted operating income growth of 2.0%–4.0%. The $0.64 EPS consensus is at the top of the range, assuming a comparable adjusted basis.

The note makes the outlook part of its clean-beat test but omits the baseline: Walmart raised its FY27 outlook last quarter and guided to adjusted EPS of $2.80–$2.87, constant-currency net sales growth of 4.0%–5.0%, and constant-currency adjusted operating income growth of 7.0%–8.5%.

The operating-profit test lacks relevant Q2 context: reported operating income rose 28.8%, versus 17.4% on an adjusted constant-currency basis. The release says the latter still included tariff refunds partly offset by price investments; excluding that net impact, underlying growth was at the top end of guidance.
The note omits the estimated earnings timing: November 19, 2026, before market open.
The note gives the 50% up rate after EPS beats without the sample size or the overall comparison: shares rose after 5 of 10 beats and after 42% of the 12 earnings events overall.

The claim that revenue, operating profit, and outlook are more likely to determine the reaction is not established by the listed facts. The reaction history is broken down by EPS beats and misses, not by surprises in those other metrics. Present them as factors to watch rather than as demonstrated drivers.

The quoted Q2 release supplies the current Q3 FY27 guidance: adjusted EPS of $0.62–$0.64, constant-currency net sales growth of 3.0%–3.75%, and constant-currency adjusted operating income growth of 2.0%–4.0%. The $0.64 consensus equals the top of the EPS range numerically; whether it is a like-for-like comparison remains unconfirmed.

The note discusses an improved outlook as a potential catalyst but omits that Walmart already raised its FY27 outlook in the Q2 release. The current full-year adjusted EPS range of $2.80–$2.87 is the baseline for assessing any further raise.

The clean-beat framework focuses on below-the-line items but omits a material operating driver: Q2 adjusted constant-currency operating income growth of 17.4% included tariff refunds partly offset by price investments. Management said underlying growth without that net benefit was at the top end of guidance and that its outlook continued to prioritize using remaining refunds for price investments.
The reaction analysis cites the 50% up rate after EPS beats but omits the unconditional benchmark: shares rose on day one in 42% of the 12 past prints, or 45% after shrinkage toward 50%.

The valuation discussion uses the 46.0x trailing GAAP P/E to temper the run-up signal but omits the 49.9x multiple based on annualizing next-quarter consensus EPS. The latter is a single-quarter run-rate measure, not a full-year forward P/E.
The note does not state the earnings event timing: November 19, 2026, before market open, with the date listed as estimated rather than confirmed.

problems: The scenario weights (25%/55%/20%) have no stated basis. The scenarios also lack a common forward horizon and reference price: the bear case calls for the initial selloff to extend even though the note documents a day-five reversal.

The note omits the November 20 close of $342.51 and the 38.2x trailing P/E versus a 36.5x three-year median. Without that context, it is hard to judge what the rebound has already priced in or what would change the view.

The operating analysis misses a 2.2 percentage-point sequential gross-margin decline, from 50.1% to 47.9%. It also leaves the sequential iPhone and Services gains unquantified and does not flag Greater China's sequential revenue decline.

The opening gap is compared with a historical close-to-close day-one average. Those are different measurement windows; the close-to-close comparison is the like-for-like benchmark.

The KPI paragraph reproduces a long, contradictory tracker list. A clearer summary would note that both releases contain product and geographic breakdowns, so the tracker does not establish a disclosure change.

section.title: Quality of the print
section.markdown:
- **Period and EPS basis:** The XBRL figures are for [[fact:print.period|FY2026 Q4]], ended [[fact:print.period_end|2026-09-26]]. GAAP diluted EPS rose to [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap|$2.10]] from [[fact:print.eps_diluted_gaap_py|$1.84]] a year earlier. Provider-basis EPS was [[fact:actual.eps|$2.05]]; the provider-minus-GAAP gap was [[fact:quality.nongaap_gap|$-0.05]]. No adjustment reconciliation is supplied, so the gap cannot be attributed to specific items.
- **Revenue and a lower tax rate supported earnings growth, but operating margin compressed.** Revenue rose [[fact:print.revenue_yoy|+11.7%]] year over year and [[fact:print.revenue_qoq|+4.6%]] sequentially. Gross margin improved to [[fact:print.gross_margin|47.9%]] from [[fact:print.gross_margin_py|47.2%]] a year earlier but remained below the FY2026 Q1 level of [[fact:quality.gm_trend_start|48.2%]]. Operating income increased to [[fact:print.operating_income|$35.63B]] from [[fact:print.operating_income_py|$32.43B]], even as operating margin fell to [[fact:print.operating_margin|31.1%]] from [[fact:print.operating_margin_py|31.6%]]. Pretax income rose to [[fact:print.pretax_income|$36.13B]] from [[fact:print.pretax_income_py|$32.80B]], with a wider spread over operating income, while the effective tax rate fell to [[fact:print.tax_rate|15.0%]] from [[fact:print.tax_rate_py|16.3%]]. Repurchases totaled [[fact:quality.buybacks|$24.30B]], but the supplied diluted-share figures are negative and unusable for an EPS bridge. The modeled per-share contributions should not be relied on.
- **Cash flow lagged net income, and inventory is the working-capital item to watch.** Operating cash flow of [[fact:quality.cfo|$28.10B]] trailed net income of [[fact:print.net_income|$30.71B]], for cash conversion of [[fact:quality.cash_conversion|0.9x]] and accruals of [[fact:quality.accruals_pct_rev|2.3%]] of revenue. Free cash flow was [[fact:quality.fcf|$25.86B]] after [[fact:quality.capex|$2.24B]] of capex. DSO was [[fact:quality.dso|35 days]] and inventory days were [[fact:quality.inventory_days|22 days]]; comparable prior-year day metrics are not supplied. Inventory rose to [[fact:quality.inventory_days_balance|$14.54B]] from [[fact:quality.inventory_days_balance_py|$5.72B]], outpacing revenue growth, while current deferred revenue rose [[fact:quality.deferred_revenue_yoy|+6.4%]] year over year. Whether the inventory build reverses is a key follow-up for cash conversion.

The note omits useful context for two prominent figures: the +23.7% rally spans 20 trading sessions, and the 78% up rate after EPS beats is based on just nine events.
